purpose: Draft 2020-12 schema validation for the closed Design Case state, evidence, candidate, transition-receipt and rule-map schemas, and for every pre-existing governed schema in this workspace. The Solution Design core is otherwise Python standard library only.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: hand-written validators in the Solution Design core
rejectedAlternatives.whyInsufficient: The rebuild ships eight closed schemas with nested $defs, conditional allOf branches and format checks. Hand-rolled validation would be a second, weaker definition of the same contract and would drift from the committed schema files, which is exactly the failure the typed-state design exists to prevent.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: no schema validation, rely on the runtime's own type checks
rejectedAlternatives.whyInsufficient: Closed additionalProperties:false semantics are a hard safety boundary here: an unknown field in an executor-authored receipt or candidate bundle must fail, not pass silently.

provenance.maintainerNote: Long-standing, single-maintainer-led project with a continuous release history; already the workspace's only third-party Python runtime dependency before this rebuild.
provenance.note: Provenance is evidence of origin, not proof of benign content. This record admits a pre-existing, already hash-locked dependency; it neither adds nor upgrades a package.

advisoryCheck.detail: Targeted advisory lookup for jsonschema 4.25.1 on 2026-08-05 returned no advisory affecting this version; the Snyk package index reports the latest non-vulnerable version as 4.26.0, i.e. no vulnerable range covering 4.25.1. This was a targeted lookup of the two named indexes, not an exhaustive audit of every advisory source, and it is not a claim about the transitive tree beyond the pinned hashes. P1 deliberately does not upgrade to 4.26.0: the admission records the exception that already exists.

lifecycleScripts.note: Installed from the hash-locked requirements file; pip executes no lifecycle scripts for wheels, and the lock pins wheel and sdist hashes so a substituted artifact fails installation.

cooldown.reason: No new or upgraded release is being admitted. 4.25.1 has been in this workspace's lock since before the rebuild, which exceeds the three-day non-security cooldown by a wide margin.

rollbackCriterion: Remove the exception if an advisory affecting 4.25.1 appears, if the transitive delta digest changes without a fresh admission, or if the Solution Design core stops needing closed-schema validation. Removal means replacing schema validation, not silently downgrading it.
